name: Dream.Org
mission: At Dream.org we close prison doors and open doors of opportunity into the green economy. We bring people together across racial, social, and partisan lines to create a future with freedom, dignity, and opportunity for all.
theoryOfChange: At Dream.Org, we envision an America where the pathways to justice, economic prosperity, and environmental health are open to everyone. We pursue this through three dynamic programs that work in harmony to disrupt systemic inequity and build a future rooted in justice, sustainability, and innovation.Our Justice program transforms the criminal legal system by centering the voices of those most impacted. We lead bipartisan policy advocacy, community-based innovation, and national narrative change to shrink the justice system and expand second chances. Key initiatives include:-Public Health is Public Safety, a groundbreaking effort to invest in solutions that reduce harm and build safer, healthier communities.-The Dream Justice Cohort, which elevates directly impacted leaders across the country through training, resources, and strategic advocacy support.-Justice Next, our national youth-led initiative developing the next generation of racial justice leaders who bring vision, urgency, and creativity to the fight for equity.-Our long-standing Empathy Network, composed largely of formerly incarcerated leaders, continues to guide and shape our work from the ground up.We work hand-in-hand with policymakers, organizers, and community champions to pass reforms, redirect resources, and restore dignity to millions of Americans caught in the justice system.Environmental justice is racial justice. Our Green For All program ensures that frontline communities benefit from, and lead, the transition to a clean energy economy. We work to dismantle environmental racism and drive investment into communities hit first and worst by pollution and climate change. Our goals include:-Advocating for equitable clean energy and infrastructure policies at the local, state, and federal levels.-Ensuring that green jobs, workforce development, and public investments prioritize communities of color.-Building resilient neighborhoods where health, economic opportunity, and climate resilience go hand-in-hand.We are forging a future where clean air, clean energy, and economic opportunity are not privileges for the few — but guarantees for all.Our Dream Tech & Innovation program is building a more inclusive and equitable innovation economy. We work to unlock the creative potential of underrepresented communities and build the next generation of diverse tech and business leaders. Our program includes:-The Dream Entrepreneurs Network, which uplifts visionary Black and Brown founders with mentorship, visibility, and access to capital.-Workforce development programs that equip untapped talent with the training and networks needed to thrive in the tech sector.-Strategic partnerships with industry leaders committed to diversifying their workforce and addressing algorithmic bias and systemic exclusion.We believe the future belongs to everyone — and we’re working to ensure that the tools, funding, and platforms to innovate and lead are accessible to all.

rich_narrative.summary: Dream.Org faces significant financial sustainability concerns alongside low alignment with traditional Muslim donor priorities. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="[9]">Total Revenue of $5,715,452</cite> against spending that sharply exceeded income, resulting in operational deficits. The organization allocates a <cite id="[8]">Program expense ratio of 68.4%</cite>, which sits below the standard 75% charity benchmark and reflects overhead pressures. Additionally, executive compensation warrants scrutiny, with <cite id="[9]">CEO compensation of $246,351</cite> accounting for roughly 4.3% of total revenue. Despite these financial limits, Dream.Org maintains a <cite id="[8]">Charity Navigator score of 94.0/100</cite> and holds a <cite id="[8]">Platinum Seal of Transparency</cite> while executing advocacy programs like Green For All and Tech For All.
